SKI AREAS

On the mountain

Three ski areas within an hour of Kobuchizawa, from beginner-friendly plateaus to Japan's longest Highland vertical.

Sunmeadows Kiyosato

サンメドウズ清里スキー場

¥4,800/day
550m Vertical
1900m Summit
12 Runs
7 Lifts
3 green
5 blue
3 red
1 black
🚡 1 gondola 🪑 4 chairlift 🎿 2 surface

The flagship ski area in the Yatsugatake Highlands, perched on the Kiyosato plateau at 1,900 m. The gondola delivers stunning views of the Southern Alps and Mt. Fuji on clear days. A good all-round mountain — gentle greens and blues make it beginner-friendly, while the upper black runs and off-piste opportunities attract intermediates. Snow quality is reliably dry and powdery thanks to the altitude and continental air flow. The terrain park attracts a young freestyle crowd.

Snowmaking Terrain park Late Dec – late Mar
💡

Take the gondola up at opening time for untracked powder on the upper bowl after a snowfall. The summit panorama cafe has good coffee and an unbeatable view of Yatsugatake.

Fujimi Panorama Resort

富士見パノラマリゾート

¥5,200/day
780m Vertical
1780m Summit
13 Runs
7 Lifts
2 green
4 blue
4 red

🚡 1 gondola 🪑 5 chairlift 🎿 1 surface

The largest and most varied ski area in the Yatsugatake region, straddling the Yamanashi–Nagano border on the western flank. The 780 m vertical is the biggest in the area, and the long blue and red runs from the summit gondola give confident intermediates a full day of terrain. Notable for night skiing (lit slopes until 21:00) and one of the longest seasons in the region — often open into early April. The summer mountain bike park uses the same gondola and is worth knowing about if you visit off-season.

Night skiing Snowmaking Terrain park Dec – early Apr
💡

Night skiing on the lit lower slopes after 17:00 is uncrowded and a completely different atmosphere — the village lights of Fujimi visible below. Buy a combo day+night lift pass.

Yatsugatake Kogen Ski Area

八ヶ岳高原スキー場

¥3,400/day
250m Vertical
1750m Summit
8 Runs
5 Lifts
4 green
3 blue
1 red
🪑 3 chairlift 🟫 2 magic carpet

A compact, family-focused ski area on the north side of the Yatsugatake range. The high base elevation (1,500 m) means excellent snow quality throughout the season, though the limited vertical keeps it squarely in beginner and family territory. No terrain park or black runs — this is a relaxed mountain ideal for first-timers or families with young children. The small lodge at the base serves good hot soba and amazake (warm sweet sake). One of the quieter options in the region on weekends.

Snowmaking Dec – late Feb
💡

Best on weekdays — it gets busy with school groups on weekends in January. The high base means snow stays light and dry even late in the season.

GETTING THERE

How to reach Yatsugatake

🚄

From Tokyo: Azusa limited express from Shinjuku to Kobuchizawa (~2 hrs, ¥3,680). Local buses and taxis connect to most ski resorts. Car rental at Kobuchizawa Station is recommended for accessing multiple areas in one trip.

WHERE TO STAY

Ski lodges & resorts

From luxury onsen resorts with ski shuttles to value pensions with heated boot rooms.

Risonare Yatsugatake

↗
★ 4.6 (1,240 reviews)
¥¥¥ · From ¥40,000/night Ski-in convenienceOnsenOutdoor heated poolSpaWine road

Hoshino Resorts' flagship Highland property — stone and timber cottages around a cobblestone wine road. In winter the resort transforms: a free shuttle connects to Sunmeadows Kiyosato (15 min), the outdoor heated pool stays open year-round, and the fireplaces in each room become the main event. Ski storage and drying rooms on-site. One of the best après-ski bases in the region.

Book ski packages directly through the resort — they include shuttle service, discounted lift tickets and equipment rental at Sunmeadows. Popular with Tokyo families on winter weekends.

Hoshino Bleston Court

↗
★ 4.5 (890 reviews)
¥¥¥ · From ¥30,000/night Forest retreatStargazingOnsenRomanticSki shuttle

Bleston Court sits deep in the birch forest and takes on a magical quality in winter — snow-laden branches, underfloor heating, and outdoor baths that stay open even in sub-zero temperatures. The stargazing program (Yatsugatake has some of Japan's darkest skies outside Hokkaido) is unmissable on clear winter nights. Free shuttle to Fujimi Panorama Resort.

The illuminated forest walk between the cottages and the main building is stunning after a snowfall. Borrow snowshoes from the front desk for a guided dusk walk.

Pension Minami-Maki

★ 4.3 (340 reviews)
¥¥ · From ¥12,000/night (2 meals) Half boardSki storageHomelyMountain viewsGood value

A family-run pension popular with serious skiers for its no-fuss hospitality, heated ski boot room, and hearty home-cooked dinners. The owner can arrange discounted lift tickets for Sunmeadows Kiyosato. Simple but spotless rooms with Western and tatami options. Breakfast starts early (07:00) to get guests on the slopes by opening time. The best value winter base in the Kiyosato area.

Ask the owner about current snow conditions each morning — he skis the mountain himself most days and knows exactly which runs are best.

Fujiya Hotel Kiyosato

★ 4.1 (510 reviews)
¥¥ · From ¥9,800/night Classic hotelKiyosatoNear SunmeadowsRestaurantRetro charm

A 1960s Highland classic with retro Showa-era character — a 10-minute drive from Sunmeadows Kiyosato and walking distance from the Kiyosato tourist centre. Heated ski storage in the basement, Western-style rooms, and a ground-floor restaurant serving set meals. Reliable and affordable for a ski trip without frills.

The morning buffet includes Yatsugatake dairy products — local milk, cheese and yogurt. Eat well before a full day on the slopes.

WHERE TO EAT

Après-ski & dining

Post-slope soba, log-cabin dinners and farm kitchens — the best eating in the Yatsugatake Highlands.

Toramaru Soba

★ 4.4 (680 reviews)
¥ SobaPost-ski lunchTraditionalLocal favourite

The perfect après-ski lunch stop — hand-cut buckwheat noodles in a low-ceilinged, wood-smoke-scented room a short drive from Sunmeadows. After a cold morning on the slopes, the hot kake soba or the hearty duck broth (kamo-jiru) soba is restorative. Gets busy around noon; arrive at opening (11:00) or after 13:30.

Must try Kamo-jiru soba (cold noodles with hot duck broth for dipping) — the ideal ski-day lunch

Tue–Sun 11:00–15:00 (closes when noodles sell out)

Café Rosa

★ 4.5 (520 reviews)
¥¥ Book ahead Après-ski dinnerLog cabinWineRomanticReservations

Kobuchizawa's most beloved evening restaurant, and the ideal après-ski dinner spot. A log-cabin interior warmed by a central wood-burning stove — exactly what you want after a day on snow. The Yamanashi Koshu wine list is excellent, and the kitchen blends Italian technique with Highland ingredients: wild mushroom truffle pasta, Kai beef tagliata, wood-fired pizza. Book ahead for weekend evenings in ski season.

Must try Kai beef tagliata on arugula; the chestnut tiramisu. Add the Koshu white wine pairing.

Wed–Mon 18:00–22:00

Akeno-no-Soba Genbe

★ 4.3 (290 reviews)
¥ SobaRural farmhouseLunch onlyWorth the detour

A third-generation soba artisan in a converted 200-year-old farmhouse in the Akeno district. Coarser, earthier noodles than Toramaru — the juwari (100% buckwheat) variant has exceptional depth of flavour. In winter the tofu hot pot set is added to the menu, using locally harvested mountain vegetables preserved from autumn. Requires a car but worth the detour on a powder day afternoon.

Must try Juwari soba (100% buckwheat) with house-made ponzu; winter tofu nabe set

Thu–Sun 11:30–14:30

Kobuchizawa Farm Kitchen

★ 4.2 (410 reviews)
¥¥ Farm-to-tableLunchWarming dishesFamily-friendly

An organic farm restaurant that shifts to hearty winter fare in ski season — root vegetable stews, slow-braised pork from the farm's own pigs, and dense house-baked sourdough. The seasonal lunch course in winter is warming and generous. Closes earlier in winter (14:30) so plan accordingly after a morning on the slopes.

Must try Winter teishoku: root vegetable stew, house sourdough, and local Yatsugatake cheese

Wed–Sun 11:30–14:30 (winter)
